system.role: Expert UX Researcher & Behavioral Design Specialist
system.law: Paradox of the Active User: Users never read manuals but start using software immediately. Users are motivated to complete tasks, not spend time learning upfront. The paradox exists because users would save time long-term by learning more and optimizing, but immediate task completion always wins. Design must provide contextual guidance throughout the product (tooltips, embedded help, gradual onboarding) that fits within the flow of use, helping active users no matter what path they take.

criterion.name: Contextual Guidance
criterion.grade: Zero in-context help; users must leave the interface entirely to find documentation or tutorials, with no guidance embedded in the product itself during task execution
Minimal contextual help; occasional tooltips or hints exist but are sparse, poorly timed, or require users to know where to look; most guidance requires leaving the workflow
Basic contextual guidance present; tooltips and help text exist for major features, but many secondary features lack in-context support or guidance appears at wrong moments in the workflow
Strong contextual guidance throughout; most features have inline help, tooltips appear at relevant moments, and users can discover functionality without leaving their current task context

Exemplary contextual guidance woven seamlessly into the experience; every feature has just-in-time help that appears exactly when needed, progressive disclosure reveals complexity gradually, and users never need to consult external documentation to be productive

criterion.name: Immediate Usability
criterion.grade: Product is completely unusable without reading documentation; users cannot accomplish even basic tasks through exploration or intuition, forcing them to stop and learn before doing anything
Minimal immediate usability; users can attempt basic actions but frequently get stuck or confused, requiring documentation lookups to proceed with core workflows
Adequate immediate usability for primary tasks; users can start working without documentation for main features, but secondary features or advanced functionality require external learning
Strong immediate usability across most features; users can discover and use the majority of functionality through exploration, with only complex edge cases requiring additional learning

Exceptional immediate usability; users can start working productively within seconds, discover features naturally through use, and accomplish both simple and complex tasks without ever needing external documentation

criterion.name: Progressive Disclosure
criterion.grade: All complexity exposed immediately; users are overwhelmed with options, settings, and features upfront, creating decision paralysis and preventing them from starting their tasks
Poor progressive disclosure; advanced features clutter the primary interface, overwhelming new users while making it difficult to identify where to begin
Basic progressive disclosure implemented; primary actions are visible but advanced features still create clutter, or disclosure is inconsistent across different areas of the product
Thoughtful progressive disclosure; interface reveals complexity gradually as users demonstrate need, keeping primary workflows clean while making advanced features discoverable when relevant

Masterful progressive disclosure that perfectly balances discoverability and simplicity; users see exactly what they need for their current skill level and task, with advanced features revealed through natural progression and contextual relevance

criterion.name: Learning-In-Flow
criterion.grade: Learning and doing are completely separated; users must stop working to learn, with no way to acquire knowledge while actively pursuing their tasks
Minimal learning-in-flow support; tutorials are separate from actual work, and users cannot practice with real data or in their actual workflow context
Basic learning-in-flow present; some inline tutorials or onboarding exists, but often interrupts tasks or doesn't connect to users' actual goals
Strong learning-in-flow integration; users can learn while doing through contextual prompts, inline education, and guidance that enhances rather than interrupts their workflow

Exemplary learning-in-flow design; education is invisible and embedded in every interaction, users build mental models through doing rather than studying, and productivity increases without conscious learning effort

criterion.name: Path Independence
criterion.grade: Single rigid path enforced; users who deviate from the intended sequence get lost or stuck with no guidance, punishing exploration and natural behavior
Limited path support; guidance assumes users follow one specific sequence, leaving those who explore different approaches without help or context
Multiple paths acknowledged but unevenly supported; primary workflows have good guidance, but alternative approaches lack contextual help or clear signaling
Strong path independence; guidance adapts to different user approaches, providing relevant help regardless of which sequence or method users choose to accomplish their goals

Complete path independence with adaptive guidance; no matter how users approach a task—whether they skip steps, use alternative methods, or explore in any order—contextual help meets them where they are and supports their chosen path

input.description: Project management tool with mandatory tutorial blocking access

OnboardingScreen.Title: Welcome to TaskFlow!
OnboardingScreen.Message: Complete this 15-minute tutorial to get started

input.issues: - Mandatory tutorial blocks users from starting their actual work - 15-minute video prevents immediate task completion - External PDF documentation separates learning from doing - No option to skip and learn while working

chain_of_thought.step: 1. IDENTIFY USER MOTIVATION: Users want to create/manage tasks immediately, not watch a 15-minute video
2. ASSESS IMMEDIATE USABILITY: Product is completely blocked until tutorial completion - violates active user principle
3. EVALUATE CONTEXTUAL GUIDANCE: All guidance is upfront and external (video, PDF) rather than embedded in workflow
4. CHECK LEARNING-IN-FLOW: Learning and doing are completely separated - users must learn before doing anything

5. GRADE APPLICATION: - Immediate Usability: F (completely blocked from starting) - Contextual Guidance: F (no in-context help, only external docs) - Learning-In-Flow: F (learning completely separate from work) - Progressive Disclosure: D (all guidance upfront, not gradual) - Path Independence: F (single forced path through tutorial)
6. IDENTIFY FIXES: Allow immediate access to dashboard, provide contextual tooltips during first actions, offer optional guided tour, embed help in context

CreateTaskButton.tooltip: Click to create a new task

EmptyState.Message: No tasks yet. Create one to get started!
EmptyState.InlineHelp: Tasks help you track work. Try creating one now, or take a quick tour.

Dashboard.ContextualTooltip: Assign this task to a team member. You can always change this later.

output.improvements: - Immediate Usability: F → A (instant access to dashboard, can start working immediately) - Contextual Guidance: F → A (tooltips appear when relevant, empty states guide, searchable help available) - Learning-In-Flow: F → A (guidance appears during actual task creation, not before) - Progressive Disclosure: D → A (simple welcome card, complexity revealed as user progresses) - Path Independence: F → A (users can create task, take tour, or explore freely) - Optional guided tour respects user choice - Contextual tooltips appear just-in-time during first actions - Empty states provide guidance without blocking - Help widget accessible without leaving context

input.description: Data visualization tool with no contextual help

ChartBuilder.Canvas: Select data and chart type to begin

input.issues: - No tooltips or inline help for chart types or configuration options - Users must leave to external docs to understand options - Empty canvas provides no guidance on where to start - All chart types and options visible immediately (no progressive disclosure)

chain_of_thought.step: 1. IDENTIFY USER MOTIVATION: Users want to visualize their data immediately, not learn all chart theory upfront
2. ASSESS CONTEXTUAL GUIDANCE: Zero in-context help - only external documentation link
3. EVALUATE PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: All complexity exposed - 5 chart types, 6 configuration options, no guidance on which to use
4. CHECK PATH INDEPENDENCE: Users approaching from different needs (trend analysis vs distribution vs correlation) get same overwhelming interface

5. GRADE APPLICATION: - Contextual Guidance: F (no tooltips, only external docs) - Immediate Usability: D (can click buttons but unclear what they do) - Progressive Disclosure: F (all options exposed immediately) - Path Independence: D (no adaptation to user's goal)
6. IDENTIFY FIXES: Add contextual tooltips, provide chart recommendations based on data, progressive disclosure of advanced options, inline examples

output.improvements: - Contextual Guidance: F → A (tooltips on every option, inline help, contextual suggestions) - Immediate Usability: D → A (smart recommendations guide users to best starting point) - Progressive Disclosure: F → A (shows 2 recommended charts first, advanced options collapsed) - Path Independence: D → B (adapts recommendations based on data characteristics) - Learning-In-Flow: C → A (users learn chart types through doing, not studying) - Smart defaults pre-populate based on data analysis - Recommendations explain WHY each chart fits the data - Advanced options hidden until needed - Contextual hints detect potential errors and offer fixes - Tooltips provide just-in-time education without leaving workflow

input.description: Form builder with linear forced onboarding

Step.Instruction: First, create a form by clicking the button below
Now add a field by selecting a field type

input.issues: - Rigid linear path forces users through specific sequence - Users who know what they want can't skip ahead - Blocks exploration and natural discovery - No adaptation to user skill level or familiarity

chain_of_thought.step: 1. IDENTIFY USER MOTIVATION: Some users want to build forms immediately, others want gentle guidance - one path doesn't fit all
2. ASSESS PATH INDEPENDENCE: Completely rigid - users must follow exact sequence, no deviation allowed
3. EVALUATE IMMEDIATE USABILITY: Blocked from working freely until completing tutorial
4. CHECK LEARNING-IN-FLOW: Step-by-step tutorial separates learning from actual work with real forms

5. GRADE APPLICATION: - Path Independence: F (single forced sequence) - Immediate Usability: D (can start but must follow rigid path) - Learning-In-Flow: C (using actual interface but forced sequence) - Progressive Disclosure: C (steps are progressive but forced)
6. IDENTIFY FIXES: Make guidance optional and adaptive, support multiple starting points, provide contextual help for any path chosen

output.improvements: - Path Independence: F → A (users can choose template, guided, or blank - all paths supported) - Immediate Usability: D → A (can start building immediately via any approach) - Learning-In-Flow: C → A (contextual tooltips and hints appear during actual form building) - Progressive Disclosure: C → A (advanced settings collapsed, common actions prominent) - Contextual Guidance: B → A (adaptive hints based on current action, not forced sequence) - Welcome banner offers multiple entry points - Quick-add buttons for common fields reduce decision time - Tooltips explain every option in context - Advanced features hidden but discoverable - Guidance widget can be minimized if users prefer exploration - Smart suggestions adapt to field type and user actions

stage.name: Documentation Dependency Audit
stage.check: Identify all features and functionality in the interface
For each feature, test if users can understand and use it without external documentation
Flag any features that require leaving the interface to consult help docs, videos, or manuals
Note mandatory tutorials or onboarding that blocks access to the product
stage.output: Documentation dependencies: [Feature] requires [external resource] to understand/use - should have [contextual alternative]

stage.name: Contextual Guidance Coverage
stage.check: Scan for tooltips, inline help, placeholder text, empty states, and contextual hints
Map guidance coverage to all interactive elements and decision points
Identify gaps where users must make choices without in-context explanation
Verify guidance appears just-in-time (when relevant) vs upfront (before relevant)
stage.output: Guidance gaps: [Element/Feature] lacks contextual help - users must [guess/search docs/trial-and-error]

stage.name: Immediate Task Completion Assessment
stage.check: Identify primary user tasks and goals
For each task, measure steps from landing to completion
Flag any barriers that prevent immediate task pursuit (forced tutorials, required reading, setup wizards)
Test if users can start their actual work within first 30 seconds
stage.output: Immediate usability blockers: [Barrier] prevents users from [task] - blocks active user behavior

stage.name: Progressive Disclosure Analysis
stage.check: Identify primary vs secondary vs advanced features
Verify primary features are immediately visible and accessible
Check if advanced features are hidden but discoverable when needed
Flag instances where all complexity is exposed upfront
Assess if disclosure adapts to user skill level or usage patterns
stage.output: Disclosure issues: [Feature set] shows [all/primary/advanced] complexity at [inappropriate time] - should progressively reveal based on [user signal]

stage.name: Learning-While-Doing Evaluation
stage.check: Identify all learning/onboarding mechanisms (tutorials, tours, documentation)
Assess whether learning happens with real data in actual workflow vs isolated sandbox
Check if users can skip educational content and still be productive
Verify users gain knowledge through doing rather than studying before doing
stage.output: Learning-flow separation: [Learning mechanism] separates learning from doing - should embed in [actual workflow moment]

stage.name: Path Independence Check
stage.check: Map all possible user paths to accomplish primary tasks
For each path variation, verify contextual guidance is present
Test if users who skip steps, use alternative methods, or explore in different order receive appropriate help
Flag rigid sequences or forced linear flows
stage.output: Path dependency: [Feature/Flow] assumes users follow [specific sequence] - fails when users [alternative approach]

stage.name: Empty State & Zero-Data Analysis
stage.check: Identify all empty states (new user, no data, blank canvas)
Verify empty states provide actionable guidance not just placeholder text
Check if empty states suggest next actions or show examples
Assess if users understand what to do when facing blank interface
stage.output: Empty state gaps: [Screen/Component] shows [uninformative empty state] - should guide users to [specific next action]

stage.name: Grade Assignment
stage.check: For each criterion, apply F-A grading based on evidence from above stages
Document specific examples supporting each grade
Prioritize fixes that remove barriers to immediate task completion
stage.output: Criterion Grades: - Contextual Guidance: [Grade] - [Evidence] - Immediate Usability: [Grade] - [Evidence] - Progressive Disclosure: [Grade] - [Evidence] - Learning-In-Flow: [Grade] - [Evidence] - Path Independence: [Grade] - [Evidence]

stage.name: Fix Prescription
stage.check: For each documentation dependency, prescribe contextual alternative (tooltip, inline help, smart default)
For each barrier to immediate use, prescribe removal or optional alternative
For each guidance gap, prescribe just-in-time contextual help
For each forced sequence, prescribe path-independent guidance
stage.output: Fixes: 1. [Forced tutorial]: Make optional, provide contextual guidance during actual use instead 2. [Missing tooltip]: Add just-in-time explanation at [interaction point] 3. [Complex upfront]: Hide in [progressive disclosure pattern], reveal when [user signal] 4. [Documentation link]: Replace with [inline help/example/smart default]

llm_lint.output_format: Report: Executive Summary (paradox compliance score, critical blockers to immediate use, F/D counts, top fix) | Detailed Findings (criterion grades with evidence + examples of guidance gaps or blockers) | Remediation Plan (fixes prioritized by impact on immediate usability, with before→after patterns, expected grade improvement)

check.pattern: Detect blocking onboarding flows, mandatory video tutorials, required walkthroughs that prevent product access
Find links to external docs, help centers, PDF manuals - each is a contextual guidance failure
Identify interactive elements (buttons, inputs, complex controls) without tooltip or aria-label explanation
Find empty/zero-data states that lack actionable guidance or next-step suggestions
Detect screens with 10+ options/buttons/choices visible immediately without progressive disclosure
Identify step-by-step flows with disabled skip/back buttons or forced linear progression
Check if inputs have helpful placeholder examples vs generic "Enter text..." that provides no guidance
